items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Five years of administrative work experience in an academic setting.
Experience in Academic Personnel, preferably within the UC Davis School of Medicine or School of Nursing.
Experience with applying various computer programs (Word, Excel, Adobe Acrobat) to organize and complete work assignments.

The analysts serve as the primary resource on academic personnel issues for the Associate Deans, Academic Personnel Manager, Department Managers and department staff. Academic personnel analysts also serve in the back-up role for the School of Nursing. They provide analytical support for the broad range of academic personnel activities in the School of Medicine pertaining to members of the Academic Senate or Academic Federation, collective bargaining units, visiting titles, graduate titles, post-doctoral titles and miscellaneous titles in the academic arena. The analysts conduct in-depth research on complex issues and problematic cases and recommend solutions. They are required to monitor the quality of all packets submitted for academic merit advancement or promotion and provide formative feedback to the submitting departments. This position has primary independent responsibility for management of department faculty recruitments, and ancillary support for high-level academic recruitments (Associate Deans, Department Chairs, Center Directors, and Endowed Chairs) This position provides consultation, analysis, review, and instruction of the academic recruitment process, recruitment waivers and Tentative Offer Letters to department personnel. This position serves as the liaison and expert for the campus Partner Opportunity Program in the School of Medicine and provides guidance on all ancillary recruitment policies.
40% - Academic Personnel Actions Analysis and Advising
Strong organizational skills to coordinate large volumes of work and establish priorities.
Knowledge of School of Medicine payroll coding practices and use of earn codes.
Exceptional interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills to effectively respond in a professional manner by email, in person or by telephone.
Advanced knowledge of appointment and review process for Postdoctoral Scholars, Graduate Student Researchers, Junior Specialists, Visiting, Courtesy Titles, and Volunteer Clinical Professors.
Ability to work effectively and efficiently in an independent, as well as, a team environment.
Demonstrated ability to understand and maintain confidentiality in an academic setting while understanding University polices regarding the confidentiality of academic personnel information.
